name: Elmwood North
city: Denver (mailing address; site is in unincorporated Adams County)
headline: Delwest Development Corp. plans Elmwood North, 70 four-bedroom rental townhomes for families at 80% and 90% AMI at 8000 N. Pecos St. in unincorporated Adams County (Denver address), and won one of CHFA's first three Middle-Income Housing Tax Credit awards in 2025.
why_it_matters: It tests the new MIHTC with a lean capital stack (a HUD 221(d)(4) loan, land equity and $1.65M a year of state credit, with no federal credit) and a housing authority partner, Maiker, brought in for a property tax abatement. Its county plat was still in review in September 2026, well behind the applicant's schedule.

status.label: Credits awarded; county plat still in review, no closing or construction confirmed
status.detail: CHFA awarded the credit in 2025. Adams County's land use case list shows the Elmwood North minor subdivision plat (PRC2024-00012) still under review, with a fifth submittal on 2026-09-02. No public record of a financing closing, a building permit or a construction start was found. The application had targeted a Q1 2026 closing and vertical construction in June 2026.

next_step: Watch Adams County's case page for approval and recording of the Elmwood North Filing No. 1 plat (PRC2024-00012), then for building permits and the HUD 221(d)(4) loan closing.

key_numbers.meaning: Half at 80% AMI and half at 90% AMI, in five three-story buildings.
The largest of CHFA's three 2025 MIHTC awards, which totaled $4,832,748 for 220 units. The applicant puts it at about $4.9M of equity at $0.60 per credit.
The planned senior construction-to-permanent loan, from Wells Fargo per a letter of interest. It is the bulk of the financing.
The applicant committed to 40 years instead of the required 30.

Maiker Housing Partners (Adams County housing authority)

background.text: Elmwood North won one of CHFA's three 2025 MIHTC awards, the program's first year. CHFA received five applications asking for $8.1M for 419 units and awarded $4,832,748 for 220 units. CHFA describes MIHTC units as affordable to households at 80% to 120% AMI.

Delwest owns the land and is contributing it at $2.2M. The site is Lot 1, Block 4 of Sherrelwood Village Filing No. 1, the north part of the Sherrelwood Village PUD, where Delwest built 41 single-family homes in 2019 before the pandemic paused the second phase.

Local approvals: the project needs Sherrelwood Village PUD Amendment No. 2 (PUD2024-00006, 70 townhouses) and the Elmwood North minor subdivision plat (PRC2024-00012); Adams County requested comments on the plat case on 2024-07-25. The applicant expected PUD approval in July or August 2025 and building permits in fall 2025. Submittals on the plat case continued through 2026-09-02, and no county approval record for either case was found.
The applicant says the site lies on a bus corridor that qualifies under HB 24-1007 and HB 24-1304 for higher density and no minimum parking, and that the PUD amendment only changes unit density.
Maiker Housing Partners and Adams County staff wrote letters of support. Maiker also plans to include Elmwood North in its voucher referral program.
Delwest contributed $100,000 to the 2024 Sherrelwood Park upgrades next door. The applicant also pitches the units for home-based child care under a 6+2 license.
Construction costs are based on Delwest's similar Vista townhomes at Mile High Greyhound Park in Commerce City. Delwest is studying offsite (prefabricated) components to cut cost.
The July 2026 draft of the plat in the county file carries a mortgage holder consent block for Mercy Funding, which suggests an existing lender on the land (inferred).
The credit amount moved slightly: $1,650,000 on the March 2025 letter-of-intent report, $1,649,753 on the May 2025 applicant report, and $1,650,000 on the award report.
